item.title: Contouring mitigates voiding at the lithium/ceramic electrolyte interface on discharging solid-state batteries
item.description:

Nature Energy | 🔬 Research Article | 🔓 Open Access
💡 Contouring the Li/Li6PS5Cl interface with egg-box topography raises the voiding-onset current tenfold (0.2 to 2 mA cm−2) and sustains pulsed currents up to 3–8 mA cm−2 without failure. It suppresses void growth and polarization, enabling realistic EV drive-cycle discharge where flat interfaces fail. This establishes interface contouring as a practical strategy for achieving relevant discharge rates in solid-state batteries.
🏷 solid-state battery · Li/ceramic interface · void formation · interface contouring · discharge rate

Journal of Materials Chemistry A | 🔬 Research Article
💡 The novelty lies in a bioinspired "rugged mountain and gentle water" binder design combining rigid PAEK for mechanical confinement with tethered PEG for stress relaxation and Li⁺ conduction. This triple synergy simultaneously enhances mechanical robustness, adhesion, and kinetics of silicon anodes, addressing their large volume expansion and poor cycling stability—offering a significant strategy for high-performance lithium-ion batteries.
🏷 silicon anode · binder design · lithium-ion battery · PAEG binder · stress relaxation

💡 The novelty lies in using an arc-melted Ca–Zn alloy as a reproducible, electrochemically active counter electrode in Ca(TFSI)₂-based aprotic electrolytes, addressing the challenge of reliable calcium electrochemistry. item.title: Boosting Li + transport in Li 3 YCl 6 by cation–anion co-doping: a channel-widening strategy from first-principles
item.description:

Journal of Materials Chemistry A | 🔬 Research Article
💡 Co/Br cation–anion co-doping of Li₃YCl₆ is novel, using a channel-widening strategy from first-principles: doping weakens Li–Cl/Br bonds and widens Li⁺ migration channels. This lowers migration barriers and raises room-temperature conductivity to 20.91 mS cm⁻¹, offering a rational design route for high-performance halide solid electrolytes.
🏷 Li3YCl6 electrolyte · cation-anion co-doping · Li+ transport · first-principles · solid electrolyte

Nano Letters | 🔬 Research Article
💡 The novelty lies in a rapid one-step hydrothermal synthesis of H+/Na+ cointercalated hydrogen sodium vanadate with a porous nanoflower architecture. Na+ pillars stabilize the layered framework while H+ enables local charge compensation, lowering Zn2+ diffusion barriers. This dual-ion strategy yields superior zinc-ion storage in both coin and flexible pouch cells, offering a practical route to high-performance aqueous battery cathodes.

item.title: Data-Driven Electrolyte Design by Electrotopological State Descriptors for Na-Ion Batteries with Minimal Solid-Electrolyte Interphase Dissolution
item.description:
با رویکرد داده‌محور مبتنی بر توصیفگر EState، الکترولیت‌هایی برای باتری Na-ion طراحی شد که انحلال SEI را به ۶٪ کاهش داده و بازده کولمبی نزدیک به واحد را ممکن ساخت.
Journal of the American Chemical Society | 🔬 Research Article
💡 This work establishes the first quantitative, data-driven link between electrolyte physicochemical descriptors—specifically the solvent average electrotopological state (EState) index—and SEI dissolution in Na-ion batteries. High-EState electrolytes cut SEI dissolution to 6% of conventional levels, enabling 99.98% Coulombic efficiency over 1000 cycles in an all-earth-abundant full cell, providing general design principles for high-reversibility NIBs.
🏷 Na-ion battery · SEI dissolution · electrolyte design · electrotopological state · data-driven

item.title: Hexafluoroisopropanol-Regulated Interfacial Engineering for Rapid Electrochemical Hydrogen Storage of Pyridine
item.description:
اصلاح سطحی با HFIP روی کاتالیزور Co9Cu بازده فارادایک هیدروژناسیون پیریدین به پیپریدین را به 83% و نرخ 1.03 mmol h–1 cm–2 می‌رساند.
Journal of the American Chemical Society | 🔬 Research Article
💡 The novelty lies in using hexafluoroisopropanol (HFIP) interfacial modification on a Co9Cu catalyst to boost electrochemical pyridine hydrogenation. HFIP anions form a hydrophobic layer that suppresses hydrogen evolution and enriches pyridine via dipole interactions, achieving 83% Faradaic efficiency and 1.03 mmol h⁻¹ cm⁻². This enables rapid, reversible hydrogen storage in pyridine/piperidine LOHC systems, demonstrating practical potential at ampere-scale currents.
🏷 LOHC · pyridine hydrogenation · HFIP · Co9Cu catalyst · electrocatalytic hydrogenation
